news.title: Melania throws subtle shade at Trump during live Fox appearance
news.text:
Melania Trump has thrown shade at her husband’s decor choices in a candid live TV moment.

The first lady joined Friday morning’s episode of Fox & Friends to discuss her philanthropy work as well as her new Amazon MGM Studios docuseries, Melania, The Series.

However, in the last moments of her appearance, the first lady jabbed at her husband’s penchant for gold decor.

After discussing this year’s White House holiday decorations, co-host Ainsley Earhardt said: “Every room is decorated beautifully.”

“I hope you come and see it,” Melania said as co-host Brian Kilmeade joked, “This year will be more gold,” referring to the president’s recent redecoration of the Oval Office.

Melania’s response, though, was telling. She candidly replied, “Uh, not really.”

The comment comes as the debate over the president’s redecoration of the Oval Office intensified in recent weeks.

Just days after the Republicans suffered a crushing defeat in the midterm elections, Trump moved to prevent future presidents from altering the Oval Office — after he refurbished the space with countless golden adornments — by declaring both the office and the White House Cabinet Room national monuments.

“We’re going to send it over to Congress to have it ratified,” the president said, referring to an executive order placed on the Resolute Desk. “It will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people in order to build something in a slightly different shape.”

During his second term, the 80-year-old has transformed the Oval Office, perhaps more extensively than any other modern president. He has filled the room with gold accents, including appliqués, cherubs and urns, and lined the walls with framed portraits. Outside the entrance, he has added a sign in gold cursive lettering that reads “The Oval Office.”

The redecoration has drawn attention from citizens and politicians alike, including former President Barack Obama, who commented on the flurry of changes last month and said Donald’s White House looks “like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” 

Meanwhile, Donald’s new decor isn’t the only thing Melania has taken issue with.

In her new docuseries, she criticized her husband’s circle of people. 

In a joint interview for the show, the president was asked by an off-screen interviewer who was more easygoing. Donald said: “I think I’m very easy to get along with actually, much easier than the public would understand. She could well be more difficult than me.”

Melania smiled and laughed as her husband responded, but then the interview cut away to a solo moment with the first lady — seemingly set on a private jet — where she said: “He said, like, ‘Oh she’s so difficult’, but I tell him the truth.

“I feel that sometimes there are too many people around him, that they are ‘yes’ people, and that’s not healthy,” she continued.
news.summary: First lady was discussing holiday decor on ‘Fox & Friends’ when she made a candid comment
news.author: Caitlin Hornik

news.title: US intelligence chief says Trump's description of Putin as a 'friend' is 'entirely appropriate'
news.text:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Sunday it was “entirely appropriate” for President Donald Trump to call Russian leader Vladimir Putin his friend.

Clayton defended comments that Democrats have characterized as a betrayal of American values after Trump met with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for rare three-way talks. The summit last week in China seemed to be more symbolism than substance, but Trump and his top aides have described it as a historic gathering of the three countries with the largest nuclear arsenals.

Trump raised eyebrows with his warm greeting of Putin and repeated references to him as his “friend," which continued on Saturday, when the Republican president posted an image on Truth Social of him shaking hands with a smiling Putin under the caption, “My Friend.”

“In that circle — in that circle of that conversation, using the term ‘friend’ is entirely appropriate,” Clayton said on ABC's “This Week.”

He had a similar assessment on CNN's “State of the Union," where he said it was “historic” and “remarkable” for Trump to meet with the presidents of the other leading nuclear powers.

“In that context, whatever language the president wants to use, I trust him completely,” Clayton said.

Like Trump, Clayton declined when pressed to characterize Putin as a friend of the United States, noting Russia's invasion of Ukraine, an American ally.

“He is not America’s friend in Ukraine. Not at all. Not at all,” Clayton said on ABC.

Trump's fondness for Putin has been a defining characteristic of Trump's two terms as president. He beamed when meeting the Russian leader last week. After returning to Washington, Trump made no effort in the White House briefing room on Friday to walk back the comments, and he noticeably sidestepped a specific question about whether he views Putin as a friend to the U.S.

“I can’t speak to America,” Trump said, then immediately shifted to his “very good” personal relationship with Putin.

“I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship (with),” Trump said. “It’s actually very good.”

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer of New York criticized the summit as a “historic embarrassment" for the United States.

“America would have been far better off if Trump just stayed home,” Schumer said from the Senate floor.

news.title: Kushner explained under what conditions Trump would approve NATO Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine
news.text:
US special envoy and son-in-law of the US president Jared Kushner stated that Donald Trump would approve NATO Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine with Congressional approval if the overall security architecture in Europe made the need to ever invoke these guarantees highly unlikely. He wrote about this on X.

According to Kushner, Trump's willingness to consider providing Ukraine with security guarantees similar to those under Article 5 is "a key condition for achieving a lasting peace."

He called Russia's readiness to discuss such guarantees "an important step forward and a potential indication that it is serious about peace."

Kushner noted that such guarantees, together with deterrence and conflict prevention mechanisms, could significantly reduce the risk of a new war.

"President Zelenskyy is right: these guarantees must be concrete, credible, and clearly documented. This is precisely what Steve Witkoff and I are working on together," he wrote.

"These are among the most significant commitments the United States can make, and they require careful consideration. Donald Trump would need to approve any proposed guarantee subject to constitutional and Congressional procedures. He would take such a step only if he were convinced that it is fully aligned with America's national interests, and broader security arrangements make it highly unlikely that this guarantee would ever have to be invoked.

That is why security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalized separately from the post-war European security architecture. These two issues must be addressed together."

news.title: Ohio's election is over. The fight against poverty isn't | Opinion
news.text:
As many Ohioans rejoice over the midterm election results, this is the ideal moment to do something new. Let’s channel that energy and excitement to build a society where no one is left out, especially the most vulnerable among us.

Every day, hungry people come into Mercy Neighborhood Ministries in Cincinnati seeking food and financial help. They struggle to pay the rent, gas and utilities. Many are senior citizens. Most are desperate.

As members of the Sisters of Mercy of the Americas who have served the Buckeye State since 1858, we are more worried than ever before about our most vulnerable brothers and sisters. We implore Ohioans to stand up for these individuals.

Hunger was on the ballot. So was the lack of affordable housing and health care and the high cost of gasoline, utilities and property taxes. Whether data centers would continue to wreak havoc on our environment and electric bills were up for grabs.

Since Congress passed President Donald Trump’s "One Big, Beautiful Bill," roughly 100,000 Ohioans have lost their benefits under the Supplemental Food Assistance and Nutrition Program (SNAP), according to the Ohio Capital Journal.

And the state is projected to lose 51,000 jobs and $5.3 billion by 2029, when the bill’s cuts fully take effect, the Journal said. Because Republicans allowed Affordable Care Act subsidies to expire, leading about 160,000 Ohioans to drop coverage, these losses come despite rural health money from a fund built into the bill.

Connected to Ohio’s affordability crisis is the government’s spending of huge amounts of taxpayer dollars to relentlessly persecute undocumented people. The average Ohio federal income-tax filer who owes taxes likely will pay about $1,670 to finance President Trump’s mass-deportation campaign.

Nearly 8,000 people in our state were detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) between January 2025 and March 2026; less than 5% had criminal convictions.

On an average day, up to 800 immigrants are held in Ohio ICE detention facilities, a mind-boggling increase from a daily average of 117 detained immigrants in 2024. Ohio has tripled its detention centers from two to six. 

As Sisters of Mercy our mission is to accompany immigrants and all vulnerable people. Our hearts break over the ongoing harsh treatment of our Haitian brothers and sisters in Springfield, where hundreds of people now wear GPS ankle tracking monitors, a demeaning device reminiscent of the slavery era. 

Sister Carren Herring, a founding member of the Ohio Sisters Justice Network, joined hundreds of protestors outside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) field office in Blue Ash last summer as Haitian immigrants arrived by bus − and left wearing the monitors.

Isn’t the Buckeye State, once a critical hub of the Underground Railroad, better than this? More than 40,000 to 50,000 individuals fleeing slavery escaped through Ohio before the Civil War.

Because of immigration, affordability and other important issues on the ballot, Sister Paulanne Diebold held a pre-election postcard writing party at McAuley Convent in Cincinnati. The sisters sent postcards to voters statewide, urging them to vote for candidates who supported compassionate policies.

We accompany struggling Ohioans because of the Gospel imperative, “whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.” (Matthew 25:40)

The Sisters of Mercy seek to build a community where all people flourish. At a time when Ohioans face unprecedented economic and moral challenges, we urge our newly elected leaders to work relentlessly for the common good − and our fellow citizens to hold these leaders to their promises.

As the Catholic Conference of Ohio’s Faithful Citizenship Guide reminds people of faith and goodwill, our elected leaders must work for “the protection and empowerment of the poor, the education of children, access to health care and care for creation.”

Citizens statewide voted for change that benefits all of us. Let’s come together to create an inclusive community for all Ohioans.

Sister Paulanne Diebold and Sister Carren Herring live in Cincinnati, where Sister Paulanne helps care for other sisters and Sister Carren does works of mercy as a volunteer. They are members of the Sisters of Mercy of the Americas, the largest order of Catholic religious women in the United States, which sponsors Mercy Neighborhood Ministries, a nonprofit that provides senior services and workforce development.

news.title: Analysis:Europe's cloud sovereignty push gains ground, but US hyperscalers remain dominant
news.text:
Nov 23 : A drive to ensure critical digital services can operate under European control is gaining traction, industry executives say, with governments and regulated industries taking sovereignty into account when awarding cloud services contracts.

While digital sovereignty has been a political objective for years, procurement criteria and contract awards are beginning to reflect those priorities. 

The change follows a year in which European policymakers and businesses have become more sensitive to their dependence on US technology. US President Donald Trump's return to office and restrictions on access to some technologies heightened concerns over strategic dependencies, while cloud-service disruptions highlighted the risks of concentrating critical services with a small number of providers.

In April, the European Commission awarded four sovereign-cloud contracts worth up to €180 million ($198 million) over six years to groups led by Luxembourg's Post Telecom and Belgium's Proximus, alongside Germany's StackIT and France's Scaleway.

The Dutch government also signed a framework agreement with StackIT, saying it would reduce dependence on non-European suppliers and strengthen digital resilience.

Recent procurements by organisations including Denmark's state railway operator DSB, Swiss federal entities and Germany's public broadcasters have incorporated digital sovereignty requirements aimed at reducing dependence on individual providers and foreign jurisdictions.

"The sovereignty criteria are something that comes much more to the forefront in the public sector and then the leading regulated industries," said Markus Noga, chief technology officer at IONOS, Germany's largest hosting and cloud provider.

The shift is not always a choice between European and US providers. Google Cloud's S3NS joint venture with Thales, which has obtained France's SecNumCloud certification for handling sensitive government and regulated-industry workloads, was selected under the European Commission's €180 million programme.

Google Cloud said public-sector tenders increasingly assess providers on operational autonomy, control of encryption keys and cloud-exit provisions, which allow customers to move applications and data to another provider if required, rather than simply where data is stored.

"The true value comes from not being subject to a kill switch and being able to continue your operations indefinitely," Noga said.

Christine Knackfuss-Nikolic, chief sovereignty officer at Deutsche Telekom's IT services arm T-Systems, said digital sovereignty had shifted from a discussion topic to a procurement consideration during 2025.

She cited concerns over strategic dependence and operational resilience, including the temporary loss of access to Microsoft services by the International Criminal Court and restrictions on some AI model exports.

Recent European Commission initiatives, including its proposed Cloud and AI Development Act aimed at boosting Europe's cloud and AI infrastructure, have reinforced the trend.

Google said regulations such as the EU's Digital Operational Resilience Act, which sets technology-risk standards for financial firms, and NIS2 cybersecurity rules were prompting customers to scrutinise more closely who controls their data, cloud operations and critical technology infrastructure.

Nextcloud, which develops a self-hostable alternative to Microsoft 365, said demand for its software had increased roughly fivefold since the start of Trump's second term, while T-Systems said demand for its sovereign-cloud offering had risen more than fourfold since mid-2025.

Yet interest in sovereignty has so far translated into relatively few large-scale migrations away from incumbent providers.

A June European Commission draft of the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act said the market share of EU cloud providers had fallen from 29 per cent in 2017 to 15 per cent in 2022 and had remained stagnant since then, while Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud controlled more than 70 per cent of the European cloud market.

THE LOCK-IN PROBLEM

Despite growing demand, providers say migration from incumbent platforms remains slow.

"The business still lags behind," said IONOS public-sector strategist Mark Neufurth.

He said only a single-digit percentage of discussions with public-sector customers currently result in contracts, while procurement reviews and migration concerns often stretch projects across 12 to 24 months.

Many organisations remain deeply tied to Microsoft Office, Microsoft 365 and existing cloud infrastructure.

Google said customers increasingly sought cloud-exit strategies and open standards to reduce dependency on individual providers.

"The problem is that a lot of people don't like change and are afraid of migration projects," said Nextcloud Chief Executive Frank Karlitschek.

Amazon Web Services, Microsoft and Google have responded with sovereign-cloud offerings of their own. AWS said it conducted a test in October demonstrating that its European Sovereign Cloud could operate independently of infrastructure outside the European Union.

Microsoft pointed to partner-operated projects including Bleu in France and Delos Cloud in Germany.

Even companies benefiting from the trend acknowledge that a complete break with US platforms is unlikely in the near term.

"For large companies, for example, it doesn't make sense to migrate all workloads, only the sensitive ones," Knackfuss-Nikolic said.

Swiss banking software company Temenos said sovereign data and cloud initiatives were not yet mature enough for many large banks with international operations.

"We start to have pretty much all the pieces of the puzzle around Europe," said Sami Pienimäki, chief executive of Finnish software and device maker Jolla. "But it's damn difficult for a regular European, or even an educated policymaker, to see all those pieces on a table and make a clear picture."

news.title: There’s Never Enough Money for The Democrats Who Want to Get Money Out of Politics
news.text:
When it comes to how Democrats talk about money in politics, it’s like how I’d imagine OJ talking about Nicole…before he sliced her head off. He loves her; he loves her so much that he… well, you know the story.

For something they hate, they sure spend a lot of time and energy trying to get as much of it as possible. You’d think they’d take a breather after the election – even just a vacation – to let the dust settle and their donors take a breath. Hell, even cows get a break and aren’t milked 24/7.

But people aren’t cows, at least not literal cows (although, if you go to a mall sometime, you will see more than a few people giving it a go as one); they are cash cows, and they don’t need a break. People dumb enough to fall for the “Your dollar will be tripled” scam aren’t smart enough to know what just happened any more than Mr. Magoo was aware of the destruction in his wake. That makes them ripe for continued picking.

Since the election, the fundraising emails haven’t slowed.

Since winning easily (64 percent), Delaware’s Democrat Congressman “Sarah” McBride has sent nine emails begging for money. This is on top of the hundreds the “trans” Member sent leading up to the election in a race that was, for all intents and purposes, unopposed.

In the latest, McBride wrote, “Americans delivered a clear message on November 3rd that they’ve had enough of Donald Trump’s cruelty, and today’s vote reflects that shared vision for our caucus to work on: Lowering costs. Ending the war with Iran. Combatting corruption. Building a government that works for everyone. That work is already underway, and I look forward to working alongside all my colleagues to make it happen. It’s time to get the job done. This movement has been built by people like you chipping in $5, $10, $25 at a time. Will you make a contribution today to help me carry our progress into the next phase of our work?”

Nothing was built by these people giving money; Democrats are funded by the rich mega-donors they claim to be against. There isn’t one of them who doesn’t have a slobbering picture of themselves with Alex Soros, the weaselly billionaire offspring of George and a sack-follower of Anthony Weiner.

And he’s just one of many billionaire funders of these mutants. The more radical ones are from organizations bankrolled by traitor Neville Roy Singham, who lives in China and should be sanctioned and have his wealth seized for actively bankrolling riots and other treasonous activities. Nevertheless, Democrats from just the DCCC have sent more than 40 emails since Election Day.

In one, they wrote, “The DCCC nearly emptied our bank accounts building the Blue Wave -- we even took out a $23,000,000 loan to ensure our House Democrats could compete and win against the MAGA millions pouring into their races in some of the toughest elections. There is no easy way to say this: If we fail to pay back our debt, we could need to scale back our work now, in the critical first few weeks of our Majority -- giving Trump’s MAGA Republicans a key opening to thwart our momentum and claw their way back into power.”

There is literally nothing Congress does that depends on the fiscal health of a party’s Congressional Campaign Committee, which doesn’t use tax dollars. This is a lie, a complete scam, and a shameless/shameful attempt to milk morons who likely can’t afford it. You can’t complain about the cost of food and gas, then tell people you won’t be able to “help” them if they don’t give you more money. That’s what people ripping off senior citizens for the retirement savings do. It’s now what Democrats do.

The answer to how much is enough for Democrats is the same answer for everything in regard to your money – all of it, and then some. Never forget we’re up against people dumb enough to fall for all of this.

news.title: Sen. John Thune Wins 2026 Turkey of the Year Award
news.text:
Since the Ringside Politics program began 27 years ago, we have enjoyed an annual tradition. During Thanksgiving week, we announce our “Turkey of the Year” winner. Our previous award recipients have included both celebrities and politicians, as well as Republicans and Democrats.

For example, last year the winner was flamboyant and idiotic Democrat Rep. Jasmine Crockett (TX). In 2024, we bestowed the award on arguably the worst Vice President in American history, the hapless Kamala Harris.

Our 2023 winner was then-Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, the pathetically inept Alejandro Mayorkas, the worst cabinet member of the failed administration of President Joe Biden. He inherited a secure border but created chaos by removing President Donald Trump’s successful policies.

Like these previous winners, our 2026 award winner is a “turkey” in every respect. As usual, this year, we allowed our wonderful audience members to offer their nominations. While many uniquely qualified “turkeys” were nominated, one selection stood out for the 2026 Ringside Politics “Turkey of the Year,” Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD).

While Thune is technically a Republican, he has been a continual gift to the Democrat Party. Despite Trump calling Thune “a very fine man,” he has been very hostile toward the President’s agenda.

Of the 1,000 bills passed by the U.S. House of Representatives in the last term, “almost 700 still sit untouched in the Senate,” according to GOP House Majority Whip Tom Emmer (R-MN). The Senate still has not acted on 161 of Trump’s nominations to federal positions, including 25 federal judgeships.

As Senate Majority Leader, Thune led the GOP into the political ditch by refusing to end the filibuster and pass the SAVE America Act, an extremely consequential piece of legislation. The SAVE America Act requires proof of citizenship for voter registration and photo identification to request a mail-in ballot or to vote in person.

Today, only 24 states require photo identification to vote, while 17 states require no identification at all at the polls. Calling this an invitation for fraud is an understatement, and the SAVE America Act would have addressed this gaping loophole in our election system. Unfortunately, Thune showed no interest in passing the legislation despite strong public support.

A Pew Research poll found that an astounding 83 percent of Americans “support requiring some form of government-issued photo ID to vote.” This includes 71 percent of Democrats and 95 percent of Republicans.

The bill was popular with the American people and with President Trump, who continually lobbied for it to pass the Senate, to no avail. He said passing the bill should be the top “priority” for Republicans in 2026. He accurately predicted that if the bill was not passed, Republicans would face “big trouble.”

Indeed, the GOP faced “big trouble” in the 2026 midterms. With the SAVE America Act blocked by Thune, the 2026 midterm elections were not secure, and loyal Republican voters were disillusioned with a party that refused to follow through on major issues. The blame for all of this lies squarely with Thune, a do-nothing Republican leader more interested in keeping good relations with Democrat Party colleagues than in passing crucial legislation to help his party and the country.

This was not the only issue where Thune showed his true political colors. Overall, he is a moderate, not a conservative, and is out of step with a Trump-era Republican Party. His lifetime Heritage Action voting record is an abysmal 64 percent, while the average score for Senate Republicans in the last session is much more respectable, at 88 percent.

Partly because of disillusionment with Thune and other Republicans in Name Only (RINOs) in the Senate, there will be only 44 GOP Senators in the next Congress. Historically, American voters do not reward a party that fails to accomplish anything significant.

As Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) boasted, “56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago. Most people didn't think 51 Democratic Senate seats…a possibility at the beginning of this cycle.” Yet Democrats won their U.S. Senate landslide, taking historic victories in red states once deemed impossible: Iowa, Kansas, Mississippi and Texas.

Losing nine Republican Senators in the midterms is the worst defeat for the GOP since 1958. The next Congress will give Senate Democrats their largest majority since 2010, before the Tea Party revolution brought major wins to the Republican Party.

In athletics, a team with such a losing record would fire its coach, but Senate Republicans did not, as they just re-elected Thune as their Minority Leader. Sen. James Lankford (R-OK) said there was “widespread support” for Thune to remain in his position. Incredibly, Sen. Jim Justice (R-WV) claimed that Thune and his leadership team “didn't cause this problem to happen.” He complimented them for doing “a good job.”

Obviously, Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO) was outvoted in the closed-door Republican meeting. He had rightly questioned whether ratifying “all of the same leadership” would send the right message to Republicans. After the monumental Senate Republican losses, Hawley asked those who wanted the same leadership, “I don’t know what planet you’re on.”

Sadly, Sen. Hawley, most of your Senate Republican colleagues prefer to be on a “planet” where they are in the minority and don’t have the burden of leadership. They can complain about Democrats on Fox News, fundraise to Republican donors and, otherwise, enjoy the perks of the “world’s most exclusive club” without having to get anything of significance accomplished.

The epitome of this type of loser mentality is Senator John Thune, who has been in Washington, D.C. for 28 years, far too long. Thune and his long-standing RINO Senate colleagues illustrate why America desperately needs congressional term limits. With leaders like Thune, the GOP will remain in the Senate minority for many years to come.

With such a pitiful, unsuccessful record, it is easy to see why U.S. Senator John Thune was the overwhelming choice for the 2026 Ringside Politics “Turkey of the Year.”

news.title: How Many Times Must We Tell GOP Hacks 'No Amnesty?'
news.text:
Well, they’re at it again, the soft Republicans who either cannot or will not learn that the Republican base is dead set against amnesty. Now, let’s be clear about this – it’s not about immigrants per se. It’s about far too many immigrants, many of them illegal, and therefore here only because they chose to flout our laws, but who are not only taking our money but changing our culture. We have a right to decide our own culture. That’s a decision for Americans, not foreigners, and it’s inexcusable that some Republicans still don’t seem to get that.

But, of course, what they really want to get is cheap labor. It’s not about allegedly hard-working people who just want to serve their families – it’s about the bottom line for big corporations and small ones too, who want to avoid paying Americans what Americans are worth. The amnesty hacks want a serf class that will work without the wages or dignity that actual Americans demand. They also like having millions of more consumers here – do you think Target doesn’t want to sell to illegal aliens? Target totally wants to sell to illegal aliens who are spending the government benefits we pay for, and that they receive merely by virtue of breaking the law to come here.

If there’s a lesson from Donald Trump, and there are a lot of lessons from Donald Trump, it’s that the American people are sick of this. We’re over it. And yet the Chamber of Commerce class either cannot or will not accept that Americans don’t want America to be a melting pot where they have to do the melting, where they are the ones doing the melting. Oh, and where they get to foot the bill to boot.

Who are the cheerleaders for the latest amnesty push? There’s that annoying Republican Rep. Maria Salazar (FL-27) down in Miami who wants what she calls the Dignity Act. I don’t know, but if you want dignity, maybe don’t break the law, come to another country, and then expect free stuff. But she’s not the most annoying one. The most annoying ones are the ones who proudly announce their conservative credentials and then immediately do the water carrying for the donors – squish Republicans are a different kind of serf class – who desperately want illegals and legal aliens here in vast, vast numbers. In Oklahoma, you have Sen. James Lankford (R-OK), who was all in on that Democrat amnesty bill. This joke lets Democrats call it bipartisan. I’m not sure whether he’s stupid or evil, but Oklahomans need to dump this loser. What the hell is it with these red states? You’ve also got their Gov. Kevin Stitt, who’s talking about amnesty too. Former Oklahoma Senator and current competitor with Kristi Noem for being the absolute worst DHS secretary in the Trump era, Markwayne Mullin can’t shut up about his amnesty fantasies either. What the hell is wrong with this guy?

It’s not just Sooner State backstabbers doing it. There are all sorts of squishes out there, eager to destroy our country for 30 pieces of EBT cards. One of the underrated reasons why that useless scumbag John Cornyn got rejected by the Texas voters, besides his work with the Democrats on gun control and his obvious contempt for the base, was that he was positively turgid at the thought of amnesty. For these elderly, flaccid Fredocons, amnesty is their Viagra.

But the fact is that the base is done with this. It’s over. We don’t want immigration reform. We want illegal aliens not coming in, and the ones who are here deported. And you know what? That’s OK, because it’s our country. We are citizens, and we get to choose.

Neither the preferences of a bunch of third-world peasants nor the greed of a bunch of American corporatist traitors take moral priority over the desire of regular Americans to live in a country that is still America.

I just spent a few days in the Third World. I don’t want America to be the Third World. I want America to be America. And you know what? That’s OK. What American would presume to go to Mexico, look around, and announce, “You’re not American enough? Change to conform to what I want.”

The squishes are happy about how the midterm elections came out, because the Democrats want to open the borders again and manufacture millions upon millions of new voters. This is the depth of treachery among the Republican squishes – it’s not exactly a conspiracy theory when you observe that some of these Republicans are thrilled about how the election turned out. Besides, being in the minority helps them avoid responsibility, which they do like Dracula avoids garlic, and the fact that they can bang the donation drum about the liberal atrocities to come; they are giddy at the possibility of the vote on “comprehensive immigration reform” that is really just amnesty, even though they deny it. You know, if it walks like an amnesty and quacks like an amnesty, it’s an amnesty, and patriots better duck.

They also think they can roll Donald Trump. Now it’s no secret that Donald Trump is both incredibly hardcore and incredibly sentimental about immigration. He would gladly do a deal about the so-called dreamers, but what’s the deal? What do we get? What is in it for us, which is a legitimate question, and the most important one? But no one asks that. Here’s the deal: you let tens of millions of Third World peasants into your country, and tens of millions of third-world peasants continue to flood in. In return, you get nothing, except being called racist more.

We tried an amnesty deal in 1986, and Ronald Reagan got rickrolled. We were supposed to legalize the ones who were here and stop new ones from coming. Well, the stop the new ones from coming part didn’t happen until Donald Trump was re-inaugurated in 2025. A new deal would involve us getting something of value, and I have yet to hear what that something of value is to us. The outlines of any proposed comprehensive immigration reform deal that I hear are tens of millions of illegals whose first act in America is to disrespect us by breaking our laws, get to stay here and maybe even become citizens, while tens of millions more flood in. And in return we get… nada.

OK, not a great deal.

Of course, if Donald Trump bought into amnesty of any kind, that would destroy his legacy. He’s not a dumb guy. It’s very important to him that his supporters love him, but if he betrays us like an establishment Republican, well, that’s not going to go so well for him. It will destroy the GOP, ensure the Democrats get elected in 2028, and then Donald Trump and his entire family better start measuring drapes in a prison cell. news.title: Mary Lou McDonald declares united Ireland ‘never closer’ as she rallies US support during American tour
news.text: Mary Lou McDonald said the prospect of a united Ireland has never been closer during her whistle-stop tour across the US. The Sinn Fein leader delivered the keynote address on Irish Unity at the University of Notre Dame Keough-Naughton Institute for Irish Studies on Friday. She said: “This is a time when a defining chapter in Irish history is being written. When Ireland’s future beyond partition and division is in prospect. “Never closer, never more achievable, never more exciting. The question of Ireland’s constitutional future has now moved decisively into a major public discussion. “The Irish Government has at last taken a formal step towards planning for our constitutional future and last night (Thursday) the Tánaiste Simon Harris said that the Irish and British governments should open discussions on a unity referendum. These are positive and important developments.” She also said support for a united Ireland is growing since US President Donald Trump signalled his support for reunification during his trip to Ireland for the Irish Open. Ms McDonald said: “In September, during a visit to Ireland, a serving US President, for the first time articulated clear support for a united Ireland. These remarks reflected how much the conversation has changed internationally. “As newly elected members to Congress begin their term of office, I hope that we will see an intensification of bipartisan work in support of Ireland and Irish unity. I hope the White House will match this work and the words of the President with further acts of solidarity with Ireland's right to self-determination referendums and unity. “The next US Presidential election coincides with the 30th anniversary of the Good Friday Agreement. I hope that whomsoever is honoured with election to the leadership of this country will take office with a clear policy of advocacy for and support for a United Ireland." She added: “The contribution of the United States was crucial in the peace process and it can now play an influential and constructive role on the road to Irish unity - supporting a peaceful, democratic process, encouraging confidence across communities and helping ensure that, if people choose Irish unity, it succeeds for everyone.” Ms McDonald visited Notre Dame University in Indiana, Chicago and New York last week. But she was forced to pull out of an Irish unity event in New York City on Thursday due to a last-minute schedule change. McDonald was expected to chair the Friends of Sinn Fein conference in Midtown Manhattan, New York, to speak about building a new and united Ireland. However, McDonald remained in Dublin for a Dail vote on Wednesday night, and traveled to the US on Thursday. She missed the Irish unity event on Thursday afternoon but recorded a podcast at the Ireland Rising event at The Dead Rabbit, an Irish bar in downtown Manhattan, on Thursday evening. The sold-out event was packed to capacity and some of McDonald's own team were unable to access the room where the podcast was recorded. She also met and greeted supporters there. Despite McDonald's no-show, around 28 supporters attended the Friends of Sinn Fein event and heard Belfast West MP Paul Maskey speak about the party's goal of achieving a united Ireland. Speaking in New York City, Maskey said: "Donald Trump has already said that he's in favour of Irish Unity," Maskey, 59, said, referring to the U.S. president's past remarks. "And I think that's probably the first time we've ever heard an American president say that," added Maskey. "And I think that's something to be built on. So I do believe where we have people from around the world, especially governments, there's presence here in the United States or other presence across the world. "And the more people we can get to say that Irish unity is a good thing, then the more pressure goes on the British government to ensure that a referendum is held both in the North of Ireland and, indeed, the Irish government holds the referendum in the South of Ireland as well." Maskey, who has been a MP for Belfast West since 2011, said that a united Ireland is the reason why "I get up out of bed for every single day." He added, "My aspiration is for Irish unity. I think it would be an absolutely first-class thing where we unite our country, but we also unite the people." "Ireland for too long has been defeated," Maskey added. "There's conflict that has been there at the end of Ireland for many generations." "I think Irish unity would be a really good thing where everybody is an equal," he continued. "So we can't leave anybody behind. We have to ensure that everybody is brought together for the cause of Irish freedom." news.title: San Francisco 49ers star Nick Bosa targeted with foul-mouthed chant in Mexico City after controversial comments about local fans
news.text:
San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa wasn't warmly received by fans in Mexico City after criticizing the Mexican sporting culture before a Sunday Night Football clash with the Minnesota Vikings.

The game kicked off at the iconic Estadio Azteca and marks the first time the Niners were back in CDMX since 2022. In the lead up to this game, Bosa reflected on his past experience in the country – but offered up a condescending critique of their manner of support.

'Yeah, I kind of want … I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer,' Bosa said earlier in the week. 

'Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them — no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques — but if they can cheer when we're on defense, that would be great.' 

Fans in Mexico were not receptive to the critiques of Bosa, who has been accused in the past of using racial and homophobic slurs and has been open about his support of President Donald Trump.

As Bosa stepped onto the field for the game, boos and whistles descended on him – as well as chants of '¡Culero!' – loosely translating to 'a**hole' in Mexican Spanish. The jeering continued when the game began.

The NFL has played in Mexico multiple times throughout its history, with the sport being broadcast in the country for over six decades. The first time the league visited was in 1978 for an exhibition game between the New Orleans Saints and the Philadelphia Eagles.

That 1978 matchup was one of seven preseason games which were held in Mexico, along with six previous regular season games.

The first regular season game in Mexico featured the 49ers as they lost to the Arizona Cardinals in 2005.

Games have been played south of the border more consistently over the last decade, with contests held in 2016, 2017, 2019 and 2022 before Sunday evening's contest.

San Francisco has taken part in three of those seven games, leading to a strong following of 49ers fans in Mexico. 

Helena Gutierrez, a businesswoman wearing a Niners jersey, told the Associated Press: 'I don't know why if he is coming to a foreign country that he needs to criticize us like that. I am a Niner fan for life, but I think he should be able to adapt to different fan cultures.'

The 49ers won the game with ease, dominating from the beginning to improve to 9-1 with a 35-10 win over Minnesota.
news.summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa wasn't warmly received by fans in Mexico City after criticizing the Mexican sporting culture before a Sunday Night Football clash with the Vikings.

news.title: Vance declines to say he would have ordered strikes on Iran
news.text:
US Vice President JD Vance has refused to say whether he would have authorised strikes on Iran to stop it developing a nuclear weapon, despite President Donald Trump urging him to confirm the attacks were necessary and that he would repeat the decision.

Speaking alongside Mr Trump at a White House press conference on Friday, Mr Vance said the February operation had been the president’s decision and that his own responsibility was to support him.

“The president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again,” Mr Vance said. “And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States.”

His comments highlighted the political difficulty the vice president and Republicans face as the conflict with Iran becomes a domestic issue ahead of the midterm elections.

In a post-election assessment, Mr Vance blamed the war for what he described as historic Republican losses and argued that the United States should leave the conflict. The comments were widely interpreted as a break with Mr Trump as Mr Vance considers a possible 2028 presidential campaign.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Mr Vance wrote on social media. “The president himself said so last night. If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay.”

Mr Trump said on Friday that he was not unhappy with Mr Vance’s conclusion, but believed it should have included an explicit endorsement of the strikes.

“People that work for me, they have a right to their opinion,” Mr Trump said. “But I say, I know the Iranians, and, frankly, they’re crazy.”

Asked whether the war had been worth the Republicans’ significant congressional losses, Mr Vance did not directly support the operation. Instead, he defended the objective of preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

“What I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing,” he said. “It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage, or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, potentially of innocent people.”

Mr Vance has opposed the war for a long time and served as Washington’s main representative in peace negotiations. He brokered a provisional truce over the summer, but it broke down soon afterwards.

In recent weeks, he had also sent personal messages to hardliners in Tehran in an effort to restart talks. Mr Trump ended those contacts shortly after Mr Vance published his post-campaign analysis, instructing him to concentrate on domestic policy.

“We don’t need a deal with Iran,” Mr Trump wrote on social media. “Those days have long since passed.”

Mr Trump returned on Thursday from a four-day diplomatic trip to Asia, which ended with an unprecedented trilateral meeting involving Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

He was criticised for meeting both leaders and exchanging warm greetings with them. Mr Trump hugged Xi after arriving in China and described Putin as “my friend”.

White House officials defended the meeting as evidence of mature statesmanship and said Mr Trump’s relationships with US adversaries demonstrated Washington’s global strength.

Mr Vance, who stayed in Washington, strongly supported the trip, joking that remaining at home while Mr Trump travelled was like the 1990 family comedy film “Home Alone”.

“It’s amazing what’s possible when you give diplomacy a real chance,” he wrote on Thursday.

news.title: Democrats secure biggest US House majority in decades after North Carolina upset
news.text:
Democrats have won their largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992 after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The result was called on Sunday, with Hubbard winning by 330 votes after 99% of ballots had been counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also took control of the Senate.

Democrats have now won at least 258 House seats, compared with at least 173 for Republicans, while four races remain undecided. Neither party has won as many House contests since 1992, when Bill Clinton became president and Democrats secured 258 seats.

The North Carolina result followed a recount requested by Foxx. She has represented the state’s 5th Congressional District since 2005, and state law permits a recount when the winning margin is below 1%.

Speaking to the BBC News Channel after the result, Hubbard said: “I think the American people are just sick of what’s going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change.”

He also promised to work with fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Hubbard said on X that he had spoken to Foxx, who had “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process”.

“I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework,” he added. “We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District.”

Foxx said in a statement: “After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I’m humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short.”

Hubbard had lost to Foxx by nine percentage points in the 2024 midterms. His victory came after Democrats also won several traditionally Republican districts in South Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Iowa.

As with many Democratic campaigns during the midterms, Hubbard focused on the rising cost of living in the US during the war with Iran, which was a major concern for voters.

President Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both suggested that inflation linked to the war in Iran was probably responsible for Republican losses.

According to his website, Hubbard has also pledged to prioritise working families and small businesses, support public education and widen access to affordable healthcare.

The remaining House races yet to be called are in Tennessee and Minnesota, while two elections in Louisiana will be decided by runoffs in December. In Tennessee’s fourth district, Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than 300 votes. Democrat Jake Johnson is ahead by fewer than 500 votes in Minnesota’s first district.

With control of the House and Senate, Democrats could investigate conflicts of interest and other actions involving the president and people close to him. The Senate can also approve or reject presidential cabinet and judicial nominations.

A Democratic majority would make it easier to pass legislation through Congress, although President Trump would still need to sign any bill for it to become law. His ability to veto legislation means Democratic control of both chambers would still have limits.

news.title: Seattle airport ‘outraged’ after ICE arrests two passengers during boarding
news.text:
The Port of Seattle has condemned the arrest of two passengers by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

The man and woman, both Mexican nationals, were detained on Saturday morning as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles. ICE said they had allegedly overstayed their visas.

The agency identified them as Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who are father and daughter. ICE said other travellers “began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers” during Mendoza’s arrest, describing that as “a federal crime and a felony”.

It also alleged that Mejia “hurled hot coffee on the officers” and would be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

The Port of Seattle said it was “outraged” by what happened, while Alaska Airlines said it had not received “appropriate notice of the enforcement action”.

The airline added that it was “concerned” about the arrests and understood “how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests”. Alaska Airlines and the port, which owns and operates the airport, are investigating whether the correct procedures were followed.

“Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge,” the port said.

Olia Catala, a lawyer representing both passengers, told local NBC affiliate King 5 News that they had “absolutely no criminal history”.

“They’re not fugitives. They’re going through a legal process,” she said.

The family has reportedly said the ICE officers were wearing plain clothes and approached the pair without identifying themselves.

“You can imagine if somebody’s running at you who is not dressed as an officer, you don’t know who they are,” Catala said. “So, there was a lot of panic, a lot of chaos, officers grabbing her, coffee spilling.”

Footage recorded by witnesses appears to show two masked agents wearing plain jackets and khaki trousers. John Gaedeke, who was also boarding the flight, told Reuters he initially believed the men were passengers and said they “didn’t have any identification”.

He said the agents “pointed and then they said now, and then they just lunged forward, didn’t identify themselves” before “tackling” a man.

“Coffee definitely went flying, but to me, it looked like the passenger was holding it in their hand, and when they were tackled, it went everywhere. I didn’t see anyone throw coffee,” Gaedeke said.

The Port of Seattle said it had repeatedly sought agreement with local federal immigration authorities over procedures at the airport and was discussing with the Department of Homeland Security whether any had been breached.

Its website says federal agents can access airport property and that port officials cannot interfere with their operations. It also says the port has not historically received advance notice of immigration enforcement carried out there.

Alaska Airlines said it was “required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials”. It added: “We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible.”

Washington Democratic Governor Bob Ferguson said ICE was “completely out of control” and called for immigration enforcement and border security that was “effective, ethical, and humane”. He added: “It is beyond reform.”

Katie Garrow of MLK Labor said the incident had been so upsetting to workers that four of the six crew members chose not to operate the flight.

Deportations of people found to be in the US illegally have increased significantly under Donald Trump’s presidency, while ICE tactics have caused discomfort even among some supporters of stricter immigration controls. Raids have also sparked controversy in cities including Minneapolis, Minnesota, where ICE agents killed Renee Good and Alex Pretti earlier this year.

news.title: Trump's Director of National Intelligence squirms as he is pressed over whether Putin is 'a friend' to the USA
news.text:
US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton denied on Sunday that Russian President Vladimir Putin is a 'friend' to America – though he said it was 'entirely appropriate' for the president to use the term.

President Donald Trump had referred to the Russian leader as his friend last week as the two world leaders met with Chinese President Xi Jinping for historic trilateral nuclear talks.

He then repeated the message on his Truth Social page on Saturday, sharing a photo of himself shaking Putin's hand with the caption: 'My friend.'

But when asked on Sunday whether Putin could be considered a friend to the United States, Clayton said no.

'He is not America's friend in Ukraine, not at all. Not at all,' he told Jonathan Karl on ABC News.

However, he said it was 'entirely appropriate' for the president to use the terminology following the summit.

Clayton explained that the photo Trump shared on social media 'was in context of the three main nuclear powers getting together and saying, "We cannot have a nuclear incident."'

'It's unbelievable that the three of them got together and had that discussion in what I would say is, you know, a time in the world where there's conflict and the like, and it should be assuring that you have the three world nuclear powers getting together and saying, "We're not going to go in that direction."'

When Karl then pressed Clayton on Trump's describing Putin as a 'friend,' Clayton suggested: 'In the circle of that conversation, using the term "friend" is entirely appropriate.'

Earlier on Sunday, Clayton made similar remarks in an interview with CNN's State of the Union as he dismissed Trump's caption.

'The president is the greatest conductor of foreign policy in a very challenging time that we have seen,' Clayton said.

'Getting the three nuclear powers together and getting them to agree that they are not going to escalate, that they are going to communicate, that is historic. That is remarkable,' he continued.

'And in that context, whatever language the president wants to use, I trust him completely.' 

Following last week's summit, the trio of world leaders issued a joint 'peace declaration,' vowing to uphold 'strategic stability and international security.'

The three world leaders had discussed nuclear disarmament as the globe's three biggest nuclear powers.

In a joint statement, they declared a 'nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought' and vowed to 'engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation.'

The leaders also agreed to boost global oil supplies, in a move that could raise the prospect of sanctions relief for Moscow, with increased Russian oil exports potentially forming part of a wider deal to boost global fuel levels. 

Oil supplies have been hit by Trump's war with Iran. The shortage has been compounded by Putin's war with Ukraine, which has seen Russian fuel refineries hit. 

The three leaders further agreed on reform for a more effective United Nations, and said that the International Criminal Court, which has charged Putin with alleged war crimes, and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to a joint declaration.

'The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials are of paramount importance,' it said.

But Trump's remarks about Putin being a 'friend' earned international scrutiny amid the war in Ukraine. 

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and controls about a fifth of the country's territory. Putin has shown no sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine surrender all of its eastern Donbas region in exchange for peace. 

'Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be,' Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said it was 'up to President Trump on how to call Putin' but 'for us he is an enemy... for us, he is a killer.'

His comments came amid what Zelensky said was Russia's largest attack on Ukraine this year.

At least nine people were killed Friday in strikes that targeted bridges in the capital of Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine, including 110 missiles and more than 400 drones. 

The death and destruction came after a furious Putin vowed his strikes would be 'far more painful than anything the Kyiv regime has done to the [Crimean] bridge' – his prestigious $3.6 billion crossing, which Ukrainian forces struck earlier in the week.

Yet Trump made no effort in the White House briefing room on Friday to walk back his comments about Putin being a friend, as he noticeably sidestepped a specific question about whether he views Putin as a friend to the US as a whole.

'I can't speak to America,' Trump said, before immediately shifting to his 'very good' personal relationship with Putin.

'I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship (with),' Trump said. 'It's actually very good.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and the White House for comment.
news.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton had an interesting response to President Donald Trump referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin as a 'friend.'

news.title: Alice Huang stayed in contact with Chinese spy agency during her affair with Nvidia chief – NYT
news.text:
Alice Huang, the Chinese woman central to Nvidia's recent scandal, maintained contact with an official from Beijing’s primary spy agency for over a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

Alice Huang communicated with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security between the spring of 2025 and the autumn of this year, the report stated, citing people familiar with intelligence briefings. 

A spokesperson for Jensen Huang declined to comment, while Nvidia’s representatives and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Alice Huang couldn’t be reached for comment.

Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia client accounting for billions in chip sales. 

US authorities have investigated Megaspeed since 2024 over allegations it smuggled advanced Nvidia AI chips to China.

The report on Sunday followed growing scepticism among US officials regarding initial claims that Alice Huang was a spy, first reported by the newspaper on 29 October. 

That article sparked a scandal leading to Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia's share price.

US officials have repeatedly noted that they have not concluded Alice Huang spied for China. Attorney general Todd Blanche said earlier this month the Justice Department had not yet established whether she was a Chinese spy. 

Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, repeated that point on Sunday. "Attorney general Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters," Clayton told CNN. "And I'm going to let that investigation play out."

The fallout has also prompted scrutiny of Washington's export controls on China, with lawmakers questioning whether the Donald Trump administration has been too lax regarding semiconductor regulations. 

The affair itself is of less interest, Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told the NBC. "I hope he had a good time," Kennedy said on Sunday. "It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy."
news.summary: Suspected spy reportedly communicated with China's Ministry of State Security between spring of 2025 and autumn of this year

news.title: 2027: Tinubu can’t save Alli, Yayi, Hamzat – Opposition
news.text:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo states are regrouping and intensifying mobilisation to secure victory for the party’s governorship candidates following President Bola Tinubu’s endorsement at Saturday’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The renewed push by the ruling party comes as seven opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party, African Democratic Congress, Labour Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Movement and Young Progressives Party, also move to strengthen their electoral prospects in the three South-West states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The development has set the stage for a fierce political contest, with APC leaders seeking to consolidate support for their candidates and translate the President’s endorsements into electoral victories, while opposition parties insist they are determined to defeat the ruling party at the polls.

The APC is particularly keen to retain control of Lagos and Ogun states while wresting Oyo State from the opposition, with party leaders stepping up efforts to rally members and supporters behind the three governorship candidates.

At Saturday’s rally held at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Tinubu publicly endorsed Senator Sharafadeen Alli, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and Obafemi Hamzat as the APC governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, respectively.

The President raised the candidates’ hands in a symbolic show of support, telling the gathering, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before presenting Alli to the crowd.

He also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South.

The endorsements have given fresh impetus to the ruling party’s campaign efforts in the three states, with the APC seeking to capitalise on the President’s political influence and mobilise support for its candidates.

However, opposition parties have dismissed the endorsements as insufficient to guarantee electoral victories, insisting that the ruling party would face stiff resistance in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In separate exclusive interviews with The PUNCH on Sunday, representatives of the seven opposition parties argued that Tinubu’s backing would not automatically translate into votes, maintaining that the electorate would ultimately determine the outcome of the governorship elections.

Some of the parties described the endorsements as a potential electoral liability, arguing that dissatisfaction with the APC’s performance could undermine the chances of its candidates.

The SDP National Publicity Secretary, Rufus Aiyenigba, said Tinubu’s endorsement posed no threat to the electoral prospects of his party’s candidates.

He said, “The President’s endorsements are not in any way a threat to the chances of the candidates of the SDP. The Nigerian people will surely make their choices and rightly at the polls.”

Similarly, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said the APC had lost the confidence of Nigerians, arguing that no number of endorsements could reverse the ruling party’s declining popularity.

He said, “APC has lost the trust and confidence of the people. No matter the number of endorsements, they have been massively rejected by the majority of Nigerians for their woeful failure and poor performance.

“The NDC is the preferred party by the people, and we shall win by a landslide in most of the states in the coming general elections.”

The Labour Party National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, went further, describing Tinubu’s endorsement as potentially counterproductive, given what he called the President’s poor performance in office.

Asogwa said although the President had the right to support candidates of his party, the electorate retained the power to decide their political fate.

He said, “The President has the right to endorse the candidates of his party, while the electorate has the ultimate right to decide on election day. How can the Labour Party be bothered by the endorsement made by a President whose record of performance is abysmally poor? Such an endorsement is counterproductive and an own goal against the endorsees.

“We all saw what happened in America recently, where several Republican candidates endorsed by Donald Trump lost elections in the midterms. The few who managed to win were those who were wise enough to extricate themselves from the failures of the Trump presidency. 

“So, I am sure the candidates would secretly be cursing the President for bringing misfortune to their campaigns and chances of winning. Meanwhile, in Lagos, where we have Hamzat, who jointly supervised the pillaging of the state’s resources for the past eight years, what is he coming to tell Lagosians?

“The Labour Party candidate in Lagos, Rotimi Odunaike, is speaking to Lagosians, and the preponderance of opinion on the streets of Lagos is that he should be given a chance to come in and turn his dreams into reality.”

In Ogun State, the PDP also dismissed the significance of Tinubu’s endorsement of Yayi, insisting that residents had already made up their minds to vote for the party’s governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu.

The Media Aide to Adebutu, Afolabi Orekoya, told our correspondent on Sunday that the President’s endorsement would not alter the political calculations in the state.

He said, “The endorsement of governorship candidates of Ogun, Oyo and Lagos by President Bola Tinubu during his campaign at Ibadan on Saturday has nothing to do with the chances of the PDP governorship candidate for Ogun State in person of Hon Oladipupo Adebutu.

“It has absolutely nothing to do with our candidate because it is not the President who will come around to vote in the state. The duty of voting in the next governor for the state is purely the prerogative of the residents of Ogun State, and the people are already talking daily that they are pitching their tent with the PDP.

“It is the people that will decide; they are the ones to determine the chances of everyone, and we are happy with the position that the people of the state are taking every day. They are confident that with the PDP back in power, all of this anguish and hardship foisted on them by the APC will become a thing of the past.

“Our campaign watchword is Itura De, meaning that relief is here. So, let the President endorse anybody; it is none of our business because we know that the people have taken their destiny into their hands to ensure that the next party in power in the state is PDP.

“By the special grace of God, the PDP is winning all 26 State House of Assembly members; we are winning all the House of Representatives and the three Senate seats.

“And for the governorship, PDP will clear all six local governments in Ogun Central; we shall clear all nine local governments in Ogun East and in Ogun West we are confident of winning three local governments. So Hon Oladipupo Adebutu will emerge victoriously as the next governor of the state come February 2027.”

The PDP State Publicity Secretary, Kayode Adebayo, also dismissed the endorsement, saying it would not give the APC any electoral advantage in the state.

He said, “Endorsement means nothing and cannot have any political advantage in the 2027 elections, particularly in Ogun State. The people of Ogun State will decide who becomes their governor in 2027, and they are already saying that it is Hon Oladipupo Adebutu and other candidates of our great party that they want.”

Also reacting, the Ogun State Chairman of the African Democratic Party, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, said although Tinubu had the right to endorse candidates of his choice, such backing did not guarantee electoral victory.

 “I can assure you that for our gubernatorial candidate, Otunba Adebisi Jimi Lawal and our other candidates, such endorsement doesn’t pose any threat to their popularity and victory at the polls.

 “The most important thing is the underground works, consultations and other strategies we employed and our continuous efforts and strategies different from the conventional one by other political parties.

“We are already harvesting defectors across the state, and in the coming days, major defectors from NNPP and other political, professional and cultural groups will speak to the popularity of our party, the ADC in the state.”

The Allied Peoples Movement also predicted keen contests for the APC candidates in the three states, arguing that growing opposition support, voter dissatisfaction and changing political alignments could work against the ruling party despite Tinubu’s endorsement.

The APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, told The PUNCH that voters in Lagos were increasingly yearning for a change, while the APC candidate in Ogun could face a difficult contest following the court clearance of the PDP candidate, Adebutu.

He said, “It will be keenly contested, particularly in the three states. First, in Lagos State, the consciousness among non-indigenes, particularly the Igbos, to vote for opposition parties, including the APM, NDC and ADC, is rising.

“Secondly, with the new movement and political orientation and reorientation going on in the states, no matter the backing and endorsement, they may lose. In Lagos, people are already tired of Hamzat’s years in government, so they will yearn for a change.
news.summary:
Opposition parties say Tinubu’s endorsement of Alli, Yayi and Hamzat won’t guarantee APC victory in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos in the 2027 governorship elections.

news.title: Former NSA Sullivan says Shenzhen summit delivered no practical gains for US
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Nov 23 (IANS) Former US National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan has said that President Donald Trump's summit with the leaders of China and Russia produced no practical gains for Washington and sent a troubling signal about its relations with its allies. Speaking on CNN's Fareed Zakaria GPS on Sunday (local time), Sullivan also warned about China's expanding nuclear arsenal, while acknowledging that bringing Beijing into discussions on reducing nuclear risks made sense. "Did the United States get anything out of it? I would say no. Were there any practical results? No," said Sullivan, who served as President Joe Biden's National Security Advisor from 2021 to 2025. The meeting's broader message was negative, he argued, "because it suggests that right now, the thrust of US foreign policy is to draw closer to the authoritarian leaders of Russia and China than to our democratic allies." Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on November 19. Their joint declaration pledged dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation. The declaration reaffirmed that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought." It did not announce an agreement limiting nuclear arsenals. Sullivan distinguished what the three leaders gained personally or politically from what he believed the United States gained. Xi benefited from hosting the meeting and occupying the central position, he said. Putin used it to signal that major powers could decide the fate of smaller countries, undermining Ukrainian confidence. Trump, Sullivan said, "Got the vanity project of being able to sit at a table with the men he considers to be his only equals in the world." On nuclear weapons, Sullivan recalled proposing discussions with a senior Chinese foreign-affairs official in 2022 to reduce the possibility of an unintended escalation. The United States and China lacked experience dealing with each other on nuclear arms control, he said, making it important to begin conversations even if progress took time. "And he basically said to me, no," Sullivan said. He attributed that resistance to Beijing's determination to expand its arsenal before engaging in negotiations. "They've gone from under 300 nuclear weapons to now around 600, headed towards 1,000 and even towards 1500 and beyond. Basically, to get towards parity with the United States and Russia," he said. Those numbers and the assessment of China's intentions were Sullivan's. He did not provide a timetable for the expansion during the interview. Despite his criticism of the summit, Sullivan acknowledged the value of nuclear dialogue. "This is a challenge because at the end of the day, the overall kind of situation when it comes to nuclear proliferation, particularly with China, is changing," he said. "And there is some logic to get them to the table to have these discussions." Asked whether communication was needed because accidents could happen, he replied: "Absolutely." Sullivan also criticised Trump's approach to ending Russia's war in Ukraine, saying the president had returned to the view that Washington and Moscow could reach a settlement that Kyiv would then have to accept. "He's decided he and Putin will settle this war, and Ukraine should have to take it," he said. Sullivan argued that Putin was intensifying attacks on Ukrainian cities and civilian infrastructure to increase pressure during winter. "I don't think that will work because I think the Ukrainians have shown a resilience and ability to withstand it, but they are going to suffer enormously," he said. Ukraine could remain in the fight if European countries continued providing assistance and the United States maintained intelligence sharing and other critical support, he added. On Iran, Sullivan questioned whether a blockade intended to deprive Tehran of energy revenue would force it to capitulate. Iran retained ways to threaten Gulf energy infrastructure and US military facilities, disrupt shipping and keep fuel prices elevated, he said. "It would be better for the US to end the war, regroup and come forward in a different way than to keep kind of throwing good money after bad the way this policy is working right now," Sullivan said.

news.title: Trump urges Nvidia board to rehire ex-CEO Jensen Huang despite love rat's links to alleged Chinese spy
news.text:
President Donald Trump urged Nvidia to immediately reinstate disgraced billionaire Jensen Huang as chief executive, insisting his return would be good not just for the technology giant but for the entire United States.

In a Truth Social posting on Sunday night, Trump publicly urged Nvidia's board of directors to reverse its decision to part ways with Huang following revelations about his extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of having links to Beijing's intelligence services.

'I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A. President DONALD J. TRUMP,' the president wrote.

The president's appeal came despite Nvidia's board already making clear that it has no intention of bringing back the 63-year-old, who resigned earlier this month following the scandal.

It also followed fresh warnings from Trump's own Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, who said earlier on Sunday that the administration still wanted answers about Nvidia's sales of advanced computer chips to China.

Trump's latest intervention represents his strongest public endorsement yet of Huang's possible comeback, putting the president on a potential collision course with the company's leadership.

Last week, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones delivered an unequivocal rejection of efforts to reinstate its former boss.

'The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,' Jones told investors during the company's quarterly earnings call.

When Huang resigned from Nvidia on November 12, the company appointed longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and launched a search for a permanent successor.

But despite a torrent of bad press aimed at Huang - including reports of allegedly abusive behavior to his staff and allegations of further extramarital affairs - Trump has refused to abandon his campaign to see Huang return to the top job.

At a White House news conference on Friday, the president passionately defended the technology pioneer, describing him as one of America's most valuable minds.

'We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them,' Trump declared.

'I think the company if they were smart they'd take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work.'

Trump also suggested Huang should make a public apology before returning to the company he co-founded in 1993.

His support comes amid mounting pressure from Silicon Valley figures, including Elon Musk, who have joined calls for Nvidia to reconsider the decision.

A campaign dubbed 'Stand With Jensen' has attracted widespread support from employees, investors and technology executives who believe the billionaire remains essential to the company's future.

Investment firms Altimeter Capital Management and Atreides Management have also urged Nvidia's directors to keep their options open when deciding who should lead the semiconductor giant.
news.summary: President Donald Trump has urged Nvidia's board to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang, insisting his return would benefit both the company and America.
